headline_marked: Saima Wazed Putul [[resigns as WHO regional head]] amid fraud allegations
headline: Saima Wazed Putul resigns as WHO regional head amid fraud allegations
summary: The daughter of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina stepped down from her role as WHO Southeast Asia Director following investigations by the UN agency and Bangladeshi authorities.
details: Saima Wazed Putul has resigned as the World Health Organization's Southeast Asia regional director. Her departure follows fraud investigations conducted by both the WHO and Bangladeshi authorities.

The WHO accused Putul of committing financial fraud regarding travel to China and misrepresenting her academic credentials. The agency also alleged she illegally acquired a plot of land in Bangladesh.
Putul has denied the allegations. She attributed the travel fraud claim to an administrative oversight by an assistant involving $901 and stated her doctorate is honorary.
In her resignation letter, Putul expressed a loss of trust in WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, citing that she was placed on unpaid administrative leave late last year.
The resignation comes as many of former PM Sheikh Hasina's allies and family members face criminal charges or exile following the 2024 uprising that ousted the former prime minister.
The WHO is expected to announce nominations for the regional director role on October 12, with elections scheduled for January 24.
caption:
Saima Wazed Putul has resigned from the WHO. The move follows fraud and forgery allegations from the UN agency and Bangladesh.

Saima Wazed Putul has resigned as the World Health Organization's Southeast Asia regional director. Her departure follows fraud investigations conducted by both the WHO and Bangladeshi authorities.

The WHO accused Putul of committing financial fraud regarding travel to China and misrepresenting her academic credentials. The agency also alleged she illegally acquired a plot of land in Bangladesh.

Putul has denied the allegations. She attributed the travel fraud claim to an administrative oversight by an assistant involving $901 and stated her doctorate is honorary.

In her resignation letter, Putul expressed a loss of trust in WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, citing that she was placed on unpaid administrative leave late last year.

The resignation comes as many of former PM Sheikh Hasina's allies and family members face criminal charges or exile following the 2024 uprising that ousted the former prime minister.

The WHO is expected to announce nominations for the regional director role on October 12, with elections scheduled for January 24.
